standard_prerequisites.use: Lets one assume A complete with a coefficient field kappa, so that the successive improvement of generators converges.

core_obligations: (3) => (1) (proof lines 4114-4119): the completed quadric ring is reduced (the quadric is irreducible or a product of two nonassociated primes), so its subring A is reduced.

(1) => (2) (proof lines 4121-4130): A is not Artinian (m != 0 would contradict reducedness), dim(A) = 2 would make A regular and contradict the existence of q (algebra-lemma-regular-graded); hence dim = 1 and depth = 1.

(2) => (3), the lifting induction (proof lines 4133-4175): choose x_0, y_0 mapping to a basis of m/m^2 and set Q(x, y) = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2; since Q(x_0 + x_1, y_0 + y_1) = Q(x_0, y_0) + (2ax_0 + by_0)x_1 + (bx_0 + 2cy_0)y_1 mod m^4 and nondegeneracy makes (2a, b), (b, 2c) a basis of m/m^2, one raises the vanishing order step by step, and completeness sums the convergent series x_infty, y_infty.

Kernel identification (proof lines 4170-4190): the completed map kappa[[x, y]]/(Q) -> A is surjective (algebra-lemma-completion-generalities), its kernel is principal (lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2), and it cannot contain a proper divisor of Q since that would be linear and force dim(m/m^2) <= 1; hence the kernel is (Q).
proof_roadmap: Deduce reducedness of A from the completed quadric normal form.
Pin the dimension at 1 and depth at 1 by excluding the Artinian and regular cases.
Assume complete with coefficient field; run the lifting induction on the order of vanishing of Q(x_0 + ..., y_0 + ...) using the nondegenerate partials as a basis of m/m^2.
Sum the Cauchy sequences, get the surjection kappa[[x, y]]/(Q) -> A, and identify the principal kernel as (Q) by the degree argument.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the algebraic normal form theorem behind the node concept (statement lines 4089-4107). The proof (lines 4109-4178) is a complete-local-ring argument in the classical style: exclusion of Artinian and regular cases by depth and graded regularity, then a genuine successive-lifting induction that raises the order of vanishing of the defining quadric using the nondegeneracy of its linear part as a basis statement for m/m^2, closed by a completeness limit and a principal-kernel identification with a degree contradiction. H3: the lifting induction with its explicit congruence modulo m^4 is a real technique, not a reference chase.
